posts.headline: Why one CEO's troubles reach your 401(k)
posts.source: Source: Bloomberg, CNBC and AP, Nov 11 2026
posts.caption:
If you own an S&P 500 index fund, you own a slice of Nvidia.

On Wednesday night, November 11, Nvidia shares fell about 9% in after-hours trading as its board met on CEO Jensen Huang's future, Bloomberg reported. No decision had been announced that night.

Index funds hold companies by size, and Nvidia is one of the biggest. Rivals AMD and Broadcom rose more than 3% after hours.

My take: this is what concentration feels like. One company's boardroom can move millions of retirement accounts in one evening.

Do you know your fund's biggest holdings?

Source: Bloomberg, CNBC, AP (Nov 11 2026)
Educational only — not financial advice.

posts.headline: Out of work? A new rule would require five job searches a week
posts.source: Source: US Department of Labor proposed rule, Nov 9 2026
posts.caption:
Collecting unemployment could soon mean logging five job-search activities every week.

The Labor Department proposed a national minimum on November 9, 2026. Claimants would report at least five qualifying activities a week before a payment is issued.

Most states ask for fewer today.

It is a proposal, not law yet. Public comments are open for 60 days after its Nov 10 Federal Register publication.

My take: if you are between jobs, start keeping a written log of every search now.

How many applications a week felt realistic the last time you looked for work?

Source: US Department of Labor; Federal Register (Nov 10 2026)

#Unemployment #Jobs #PersonalFinance

posts.headline: More job seekers are stuck past six months
posts.caption:
More than one in four unemployed Americans has been looking for 27 weeks or longer.

In October 2026, 2.0 million people were long-term unemployed, per the Bureau of Labor Statistics. That is 27.6% of everyone out of work, the highest share since late 2021, CNBC noted.

The overall unemployment rate actually dipped to 4.1% from 4.2%.

My take: a steady headline rate can hide a harder search for the people already out. The longer it runs, the deeper savings get drawn down.

How long did your last job search take?

Source: BLS Employment Situation, October 2026 (released Nov 6 2026); CNBC

#Jobs #Unemployment #Economy

data.footnote: October 2026, released Nov 6 2026. 27.6% is the highest long-term share since late 2021.

posts.headline: A $1,000 bonus, or a $50 a month raise?
posts.source: Source: Follow the Money calculation, before tax
posts.caption:
One pays more today. The other pays more for as long as you stay.

A $1,000 bonus arrives once. A $50 a month raise is $600 in year one, so the bonus wins at first.

By the end of year two the raise has paid $1,200, and it keeps going. Future raises are often a percentage of your base pay, so a higher base can grow too.

My take: if you need the cash now, the bonus is real help. If not, the raise is the quieter win.

Which would you pick, and why?

Source: Follow the Money calculation, before tax

posts.headline: What happens to your money if your bank fails
posts.caption:
If an FDIC-insured bank fails, your insured deposits are protected up to $250,000.

That limit is per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category, so a joint account counts separately from a single one.

Usually a healthy bank takes over the deposits and you keep banking. If not, the FDIC aims to pay insured deposits within two business days.

Money above the limit may come back only partly, and slowly. Stocks, bonds and crypto are not deposits, so FDIC insurance does not cover them.

My take: check that your bank is insured. It takes one minute.

Do you keep more than $250,000 at a single bank?

Source: FDIC

posts.headline: Myth: a raise can push you into a bracket that shrinks your pay
posts.source: Source: IRS federal income tax brackets
posts.caption:
A raise cannot lower your take-home pay through federal tax brackets.

US income tax is marginal. Only the dollars above each bracket line are taxed at the higher rate. Everything below stays taxed exactly as before.

So crossing into a new bracket means your next dollars are taxed more, not all of them.

The real exceptions are benefit cutoffs, where some income-based help can stop at a set income. That is a different rule, not a tax bracket.

My take: never turn down a raise because of a bracket.

Have you heard this myth at work?

Source: IRS, federal income tax rates and brackets

#Taxes #Paycheck #MoneyMyths

posts.headline: Same 6% saved. The match decides the total
posts.source: Source: Follow the Money calculation, $60,000 salary
posts.caption:
Two workers save the same $3,600 a year. One ends the year with twice as much.

On a $60,000 salary, putting in 6% is $3,600. A 50% match on that 6% adds $1,800. A 100% match adds $3,600.

That is money added before any investment growth.

Match rules vary. Some vest over several years, so check your plan before you count on it.

My take: if your employer offers a match, knowing exactly how it works is worth ten minutes.

Do you know what your employer matches?

Source: Follow the Money calculation, $60,000 salary, one year
Educational only — not financial advice.

#401k #Retirement #EmployerMatch

posts.headline: How much you can save tax-advantaged in 2026
posts.caption:
There are about seven weeks left to use this year's limits.

For 2026 the IRS lets you put up to $24,500 into a 401(k), $7,500 into an IRA, and $4,400 into a self-only HSA.

Savers 50 and older can add catch-up contributions on top. Family HSA coverage allows $8,750.

IRA contributions for 2026 can generally be made until the tax filing deadline in April 2027. 401(k) contributions have to come out of 2026 paychecks.

My take: few people hit these caps. Knowing them still shows how much room you have.

Which of these accounts do you use?

Source: IRS, 2026 contribution limits
Educational only — not financial advice.

#Retirement #401k #HSA

posts.headline: What $100 buys after years of 3% inflation
posts.source: Source: Follow the Money calculation, 3% a year
posts.caption:
At 3% inflation a year, $100 buys about half as much in 25 years.

The bill in your wallet stays $100. What it buys shrinks: about $86 worth after 5 years, $74 after 10, $55 after 20 and $48 after 25.

That is why cash sitting at 0% quietly loses ground, and why a raise below inflation is a pay cut in disguise.

My take: you cannot control inflation, but you can check whether your savings rate and your pay are keeping up with it.

Is your paycheck keeping up with prices?

Source: Follow the Money calculation, constant 3% a year

#Inflation #Savings #PersonalFinance

posts.headline: A big tax refund is your own money, returned late
posts.caption:
A tax refund feels like a bonus. It is your own pay coming back.

A refund means more tax was withheld from your paychecks than you owed. The IRS returns the difference, with no interest for the months it held it.

If you get a large refund every year, adjusting your W-4 can put that money in each paycheck instead.

Underpaying can bring a penalty, so aim for close to even.

My take: some people like the forced saving. Just know that is what it is.

Do you prefer a refund or a bigger paycheck?

Source: Follow the Money explainer — see IRS Form W-4

#Taxes #TaxRefund #Paycheck

data.dek: A refund means too much was withheld from your paychecks. The IRS pays no interest on it. A W-4 update can change that.
